outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN) and register for the California Seller's Permit with CDTFA. What to say: Apply online for the SF Business Registration Certificate; provide the EIN, entity name and lease. The registration year runs April 1–March 31; fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k, each tier plus $4 state fee). Register for the Seller's Permit online with CDTFA (free, often same-day). Every other City department asks for the BAN, and ABC will not issue a licence until the seller's permit exists, so complete both immediately after forming the entity.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms a Conditional Use Authorization is required, file the CUA application with a project description, site photos, floor plan and outreach plan. What to say: State the use is a Restaurant (Planning Code §102) with beer-and-wine service (Type 41) as a Bona Fide Eating Place under §249.60(b)(1)(A), intensifying from an established Limited Restaurant use. Emphasize the small footprint (404 sq ft), limited cooking, no late-night hours, compliance with §202.2 and §249.60(d) good-neighbor conditions (exterior lighting, 33% window signage, 50% clear glazing). Attach a community outreach summary (pre-application meeting, letters to neighbors, merchant association contact). The CUA fee is roughly $3,150 (2026–27, no construction; fee waivers may apply for new storefronts). Budget 6–10 months including environmental review, neighborhood notification and Planning Commission hearing.
outcomes.note: The records confirm the code sections apply at the address but do not contain the rule text, subsection details, fees, timelines, or specific conditions cited.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application for change of use with plans stamped by a licensed architect, routed to Planning (§311 notification) and DPH (plan check). What to say: Submit scaled floor plans showing the kitchen layout, equipment, three-compartment sink, hand sinks, prep surfaces, storage and the occupant load calculation. Request routing to Planning for zoning review and neighborhood notification under §311 and to DPH for plan check (flat fee $828–$2,207 for a new restaurant). Include the FOG equipment specification and SFPUC's Installation Verification Form. State the prior use was Limited Restaurant per BPA #2012.10.3080 and that the intensification to Restaurant was discussed with Planning (attach the Letter of Determination or CUA approval). The building permit fee is based on construction valuation; for a minimal change of use expect $800–$1,500.
outcomes.note: The cited records do not state the DPH plan check fee range $828–$2,207 or the building permit fee estimate $800–$1,500.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the ABC Type 41 application or licence transfer paperwork, whichever the applicant has arranged, with the signed lease, zoning sign-off, seller's permit and $1,000–$1,600 fee. What to say: For a new licence, complete ABC-257 (Eating Place application), post the 30-day public notice at the premises and submit the city zoning clearance (the Planning referral approval from step 4 or 5). For a transfer, escrow the licence with a broker, file ABC-201 (transfer application) with the same documents. ABC will refer the application to SFPD and SF Planning for review; Planning's referral response will cite the CUA or the building permit approval. In an over-concentration census tract, request a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors or Planning before applying to ABC (adds 1–3 months). Expect 60–120 days for unprotested applications; protests or PCN findings add time.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the SF DPH Health Permit to Operate online, providing the BAN, Location ID (LIN), EIN, certified food manager certificate and menu. What to say: Submit at least one month before the planned opening. The $470 Permit to Operate application fee includes the initial inspection. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% kitchen completion and a final inspection when the space matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed, hot water is on, and the certified food manager is on staff. The inspector will verify hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, sealed surfaces, thermometers, food storage and the grease interceptor. A failed inspection pushes the opening by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the scheduled inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain music licensing (ASCAP and BMI), workers' compensation insurance, EDD employer registration, and schedule final inspections before opening. What to say: Sign up for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses online ($300–$2,500 each per year, formula-based on occupancy and music use); both are needed for a general mix of recorded music. Quote workers' compensation insurance through a broker or State Fund (mandatory from the first employee; restaurant class codes run 2–6% of payroll). Register as an employer with CA EDD online within 15 days of the first paycheck (free). Coordinate the final DPH inspection, the DBI building final (if tenant improvements were done) and the ABC District Office inspection before serving the public. The DPH permit is issued after the final inspection confirms compliance.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,150 to $6,500. Notes: This timeline is the time to approval when the approvals are granted, not a time to denial or withdrawal. The range assumes a Conditional Use Authorization (CUA) is required under Planning Code §249.60(f)(1): 120–300 days is the CUA alone (filing to Commission hearing, environmental review, 30-day appeal period), per the catalog entry for a conditional use in an NCT district. Add 14–45 days for the health permit to operate after the CUA and building permit are approved. The cost range covers the CUA filing fee ($3,150 for no construction in 2026–27, per catalog), the health permit application ($470) and plan check ($828–$2,207), and the building permit for change of use ($800–$1,500 estimated). It excludes the ABC Type 41 licence ($1,000–$1,600) because the alcohol row has insufficient information status. If Planning confirms via Letter of Determination that no CUA is required and the concept can proceed via building permit referral (as occurred at 2512 Mission St in 2020–2021), the timeline shortens to 60–120 days (building permit with §311 notification plus health permit) and the cost drops to $1,500–$4,000 (no CUA fee). The comparable agency referrals at this address and on the same block were approved in 7–35 days, but those were continuations of existing limited-restaurant uses; this concept is an intensification to full Restaurant, so a longer review is likely.
